<reason>A wins the incremental, net-safety comparison. B identified a plausible role for time-bound flashpoint searches and answered the review question directly, but never adequately weighed lost cooperation and diverted investigative capacity. A answered the proof-standard challenge, distinguished existing preventive action from expanded coercion, and consistently separated weapon seizures from additional reductions in violence. B’s closing largely repeated its reversible-friction-versus-death framing after A had materially undermined it. The clipped closing adds a minor execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest rebuttal was that oversight can reverse a policy but cannot reverse deaths caused by lost warnings or displaced investigative work. This directly damaged B’s central asymmetry. A then sharpened the comparison: both a confiscated knife and a lost warning require downstream behavioral assumptions before they establish lives saved or lost.</best_rebuttal>
